description: CleanVul samples whose dataset label was found wrong by manual audit against the real fix commit. Audited 2026-09-26: ALL 54 samples wrong on all 35 votes (5 conditions x 7 self-consistency draws) in static_findings_root_sweep (32 FN, 22 FP). Batches 1-4 were seeded 6 FN + 4 FP picks (Random(20260926..20260929)); batch 5 was the remaining 14. Outcome: 17 wrong labels (samples), 2 disputed, 5 not judgeable from the function, 30 genuine model errors. Tiers 34/35 and 33/35 wrong votes (13 + 19 = 32 samples) fully audited: 2 wrong labels, 3 disputed, 1 not judgeable, 26 model errors.
source_row_id_note: cleanvul_source_row_ids are 0-based data-row indices into source_csv (header excluded), as stored in metadata.source_row_ids; a sample may merge several rows of one commit.

samples.reason: WIP refactor of the return calling convention ('simplify return logic and protect return buffers from internal calls'). The buffer-clobbering guard protects the new code path; the old parse_Return/make_return_stmt has no demonstrable flaw that the commit removes. No CVE/GHSA.

Commit fixes HTTP request smuggling in parser.py/receiver.py/utilities.py. This function's delta only makes error responses always send 'Connection: close' (listed under Bugfixes, not Security Fixes, in CHANGES.txt). No smuggling flaw in this function.

Upstream CleanVul row pairs func_before = Node.__init__ (unchanged by the commit, just forwards url_fetcher) with func_after = Tree.__init__ (where the fix was added). Both are named __init__. The labelled-vulnerable function contains no vulnerable code; the real pre-fix Tree.__init__ is absent. The whole pair (label 1 and label 0 sides) is invalid.

mktemp race is fixed, but func_after of load_djpeg (row 3767) still does os.system("djpeg '%s' >'%s'" % (self.filename, path)); a filename containing a single quote breaks out -> shell injection, CVE-2014-3007, re-fixed in Pillow 2.5.0 with subprocess.check_call([...]). Model flagged exactly this.

The flaw was the active-response endpoint not validating 'command' at all; the fix adds a new format checker in validator.py/spec.yaml that reuses is_safe_path. The is_safe_path delta ('./' check dropped, '..\\' added for Windows agents) is incidental; pre-fix is_safe_path with realpath+commonpath is not exploitable for its existing POSIX callers.

Zip-bomb DoS fix only makes compression optional: _tpm2_checkquote still runs unbounded zlib.decompress on agent-supplied quote/sig/pcr blobs when compressed=True, and callers pass compressed=(agent['supported_version'] == '1.0'). At this commit 1.0 is the only API version, so every agent still triggers decompression (the code even logs 'Decompressing quote data which is unsafe!').

YAML deserialization is fixed, but toc[].file values from the attacker's mrdoc.yaml go into open(os.path.join(self.temp_dir, i['file'])) unchecked; an absolute path or '../' reads arbitrary files into a Doc the attacker owns (arbitrary file read). Model's stated reason (Zip Slip in shutil.unpack_archive) is wrong for .zip, so the verdict is right for the wrong reason.

rows.note: 10 other filesystem.py/multifilesystem.py path-conversion methods, correctly fixed

samples.reason: Collection paths now go through path_to_filesystem, but multifilesystem remove(name) still does os.remove(os.path.join(self._filesystem_path, name)) with the unchecked last URL segment (Windows '..\\' traversal). Fixed 55 min later upstream in bcaf452 'Convert component names safely to filenames' (adds is_safe_filesystem_path_component to remove()/write()); both shipped in Radicale 1.1.

Path traversal fixed via safe_join, but _get_object_element (reached from @route('/id/<dataset>/<int:seq_no>')) concatenates the URL segment 'dataset' into 'SELECT rel_path, download_link FROM ' + dataset + ' WHERE ...' -> UNION-based SQL injection. Model flagged exactly this. Same SQLi seen in the earlier function-only audit.

OAuth state check is `if state != request.cookies.get('python-flask-csrf')`: an attacker omitting state against a victim with no cookie gives None == None, so the login CSRF (attacker code -> victim logged in as attacker) still works. Model flagged a different line (jwt.decode(verify=False) on a TLS back-channel id_token, not exploitable) — right label, wrong reason.

Request-smuggling fix is validate_headers() in http1/read.py, called from _http1.py. The sample only contains plumbing for the new validate_inbound_headers option (option registration + copying it into h2_conf). HTTP/2 already defaulted validate_inbound_headers=True, so pre-fix code here is not vulnerable.

SSRF fix is validators.domain(netloc), a syntax-only check: a hostname resolving to an internal IP (e.g. 127.0.0.1.nip.io) or a redirect to one still reaches internal hosts. element() still returns send_file(..., mimetype=src_type) with src_type from the request, so attacker HTML served as text/html gives the XSS of CVE-2024-22417. Model's stated reason (pickle RCE in config) is wrong — right label, wrong reason.

Fix is a blacklist re.sub('[\!\@\#\$\;\&\*\~\"\'\{\}\]\[\-\+\%\^]+', '', project_name) before Popen('gerapy generate ' + name, shell=True). Backtick, |, <, >, ( ) survive, so project names like p`id` or p|id from the URL path still execute. Upstream later switched to argv list with shell=False. Model flagged exactly the backtick bypass.

Upstream row pairs func_before = abstract `def unwrap(...): raise NotImplementedError` with func_after = the newly added _Rsa15.unwrap (RFC 3218 random filling). The real padding oracle was in _RSA.unwrap, which is not in the row. The label-1 stub is not vulnerable; the pair is invalid.

TarSlip replaced by safe_extract, but the same function still does data['file'] = data['name'] (user-controlled) -> open(os.path.join(temp_dir_path, data['file']), 'wb') = arbitrary file write (CVE-2023-50731), and requests.get(url) on a user URL = SSRF (CVE-2023-49795). safe_extract itself uses a commonprefix check (sibling-dir bypass, ignores links). Model flagged the data['file'] traversal.

_not_here_yet still returns HttpResponse('Not here yet: %s (%r, %r)' % (request.path, escape(args), escape(kwargs))) as text/html: request.path is decoded and attacker-controlled, so reflected XSS remains (unchanged on shuup master). Model's stated reason ('arbitrary method execution' via dispatch_ prefix) is wrong — right label, wrong reason.

New _is_jailbreak only checks ast.Name ids in {__subclasses__, __builtins__, __import__}; attribute access (ast.Attribute) passes, so ().__class__.__base__.__subclasses__() ... reaches exec() -> RCE (verified locally by the auditor). Model found exactly this bypass.

Brute-force lockout is now checked before password verification, but send = request.vars.send flows unchecked into redirect(send) (open redirect, CWE-601; upstream later wrapped it in prevent_open_redirect). Lockout is also keyed on request.client, taken from the spoofable first X-Forwarded-For entry at this commit. Model flagged the open redirect.

SSRF fix is validators.url(url, public=True) before requests.get: a string-only check (validators 0.19.0 tested: DNS names resolving internally e.g. 127.0.0.1.nip.io, [::1], [::ffff:127.0.0.1] pass) and requests follows redirects unchecked; auditor reports a later advisory for the redirect bypass on the same pattern. Also BookmarkletImport.objects.filter(pk=bookmarklet) has no owner/space scope (IDOR).

disputed.reason: pickle removed, but the fix adds os.system('rm ' + filename), os.system('gzip ' + filename) etc. (CWE-78). Exploitable only if a caller passes an attacker-influenced filename; PyBlock is a library normally driven by a local user, so this hinges on the trust model.

CVE-2020-28975 is DISPUTED by NVD/vendor: the segfault needs mutating the private _n_support of a fitted model (or loading an attacker pickle, which is already RCE). The label is correct by the dataset's definition but crosses no trust boundary.
CVE-2023-0055 missing Secure flag on session cookie (CWE-614). Exact flaw is in the function but only exploitable with TLS enabled + network MITM forcing plain HTTP; hardening-grade.

Commit is a Bandit-audit refactor (not B411): Popen(cmd.split(' '), shell=False) -> secure_popen(cmd). Both are shell=False; secure_popen additionally splits on '|' and '>' (pipes / file redirection) over a mustache-rendered command containing plugin stats (process/mount names a local user can influence). 'Fixed' side is arguably worse; pre-fix label 1 is also weak.

CVE-2022-2888 session-expiration fix is sound, but merged passive_login trusts X-Forwarded-For via get_remote_address and auto-logs-in as autologinAs for localNetworks -> auth bypass when autologinLocal is enabled (non-default); later CVE-2024-32977.

pairing_issues.reason: Upstream row pairs func_before = ParseItem.__init__(self, name) with func_after = WebPage.__init__(self, parent) (name collision). The sample's label stays correct because the merged row 5636 (apply_basic_settings) carries the real fix.
func_before = _RawKeyMgmt.unwrap stub, func_after = _Rsa15.unwrap (name collision). Listed in samples as wrong label.
func_before = Node.__init__, func_after = Tree.__init__ (name collision). Listed in samples as wrong label.

not_judgeable.reason: Label defensible at commit level (GHSA-7wgr-7666-7pwj path traversal; fix added _sanitize to snake_case/pascal_case), but the sample is a pure string helper; the file-path sink is in __init__.py and not visible.

Label right at commit level (guest sent label-derived weight/sum_grad/sum_hess to the host in hetero SecureBoost), but sync_tree only shows 'send self.tree_ to HOST'; node contents and the threat model live elsewhere.

Label correct (request.args['top'] flows unvalidated into a raw-SQL LIMIT built with str.format in Song.get_related_songs_json), but the sink is in app/models.py and was not included by any context condition, so the model could not see it.
CVE-2020-7471. Sample is the 2-line StringAgg.__init__ passing delimiter to super(); the injecting sink is the class attribute template "...'%(delimiter)s'...", not in the sample.
https->http downgrade is fixed in VerifiedHTTPSHandler (not in sample); get_opener's delta is scheme plumbing, only reveals the bug if you know build_opener adds a default HTTPHandler.

CVE-2016-9910 legacy-IE attribute quoting XSS: regex contents (module level) and insecure default quote_attr_values=False (__init__) are outside serialize(); pre-fix output is HTML5-spec-conformant. Low severity.
